guidance_markdown:
## Author-provided scientific guidance

- The authors hypothesized an SN2-type explanation for formation of N-propargyl-3-nitropyrrole and performed a theoretical mechanism study to test it. Their supplied reaction account presents a connected acid-base interaction followed by the product-forming substitution; this is a proposed model-supported account, not proof that alternatives have been excluded.

- The reported reaction calculations used Gaussian 09 with the B3LYP functional and the 6-31+g(d) basis set, with SMD as the solvent model and DMF as solvent. Molecular construction used GaussView 6.0 and result visualization used CYLview.

- The displayed baseline consists of an initial reactant depiction, two proposed transition states named TS1 and TS2, an intervening state named S2 and the N-propargyl product. Figure 1 sets the displayed initial reactant to 0.0 kcal/mol and labels the vertical axis Relative Free Energy [kcal/mol].

- The authors describe TS1 as an acid-base interaction in which hydride attacks the pyrrole N-H hydrogen and H2 is released. They report TS1 at -1.6 kcal/mol relative to the displayed initial reactant, call it reactant-like and state that no energy barrier was observed in that part of their profile.

- The initial reactant depiction labels N-H as 1.09 Angstrom and the approaching H...H distance as 1.41 Angstrom. The TS1 depiction labels N-H as 1.18 Angstrom and H...H as 1.19 Angstrom; the text explicitly discusses shortening of the H...H distance from 1.41 to 1.19 Angstrom.

- The authors describe S2 as the deprotonated pyrrole state after H2 separation and report -25.5 kcal/mol on the displayed initial-relative profile. They report H2 separated from the pyrrole moiety by 3.21 Angstrom; the figure also labels the H-H distance as 0.74 Angstrom.

- The authors describe the negatively charged pyrrole unit attacking the propargyl carbon and identify TS2 as an SN2-type reaction complex. The paragraph reports a required energy of 16.2 kcal/mol for this chemical step, while Figure 1 places TS2 at -9.3 kcal/mol on its initial-reactant reference. Keep these stated local-step and initial-relative comparison contexts distinct.

- For TS2 the authors report N...C bond formation at 2.17 Angstrom and C...Br bond breakage at 2.47 Angstrom. These selected geometric observations support their substitution interpretation but are not a complete transition-state coordinate or validation record.

- The authors report exergonic formation of the N-propargyl product at -45.5 kcal/mol on the displayed initial-relative free-energy profile. The product depiction labels N-C as 1.47 Angstrom and C...Br as 3.62 Angstrom.

- The supplied reaction text and figure do not specify exact starting/optimized Cartesian records, transition-state search strategy, frequency/IRC validation records, thermochemical temperature, standard-state convention or correction recipe. The article mentions online supplementary material, but no SI document is supplied in this input snapshot. These are limits of the supplied baseline evidence, not findings about unseen supplementary files; undocumented choices must not be represented as author-reported parameters.

- The available molecular account identifies hydride and DMF but does not resolve complete sodium-counterion, aggregation, explicit-solvent or bulk NaH phase treatment. The reported profile and selected distances are model-conditional support, not an independently verified kinetic mechanism or a quantitative explanation of isolated yield.
